terms.gloss: as it were, a sort of, so to speak
terms.grammar: adverb, before the word it softens
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.43: in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus
Cic. Off. 1.54: quasi sēminārium reī pūblicae
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of excusing a bold word or a metaphor, often with quīdam: quasi ferream quandam, “a sort of iron (virtue)” (Amic. 48, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a sort of, a kind of; a certain
terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective, after the word it softens
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.10: timiditāte quādam ingenuā (Lewis & Short)
Gell. praef. 2: quasi quoddam litterārum penus

terms.gloss: in a way, in a sense, sort of
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.5.5: est mīrō quōdam modō adfectus

phrases.latin: in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus
phrases.english: in children we see sparks, as it were, of the virtues

phrases.latin: eaque mihi ad subsidium memoriae quasi quoddam litterārum penus recondēbam
phrases.english: and I stored them away as a sort of larder of letters, to help my memory
he is in a strange sort of mood

sources: Lewis & Short: quasi · Lewis & Short: quidam · Lewis & Short: modus
